Divide monotonicity of ∇V applied to q(y+tv),q(y) by t² and pass to the limit to get every quadratic form nonnegative at differentiability points. external_dependencies: Rademacher’s theorem, Lebesgue differentiation, and the Lipschitz area formula on the d-dimensional slices.

1bc960743a4bce34:02.reason: Normalize with the compact dual attainment, global extensions and finite-test compactness proof from 9c4bb3ca1bcd69e1 §§2–3,5 inlined. Its proof needs no absolute continuity to obtain Lipschitz inverse endpoint maps; hence it applies to finitely many physical fibers. The new mixed argument first proves absolute continuity of each output slice by partitioning its inverse image by the actual input base and applying the d-dimensional area formula. At density points of joint strata, all base derivatives vanish. The intrinsic pullback lemma makes the remaining matrices PSD after conjugation by the same principal Hessian block, giving the reciprocal-power formula by trace AM–GM. For d=0 the inverse map selects a single endpoint above each output point and that atom has size at most every a_i. Homothetic bodies at one base and a common atom of mass min_i a_i, respectively, attain the constants. This extends the continuous source theorem and cannot be obtained from the accepted uniform coupling, which gives no ordering relative to the old coupling.
1bc960743a4bce34:02.statement: Let n,d be nonnegative integers, n+d≥1, and let γ_i be compactly supported finite positive measures of common mass M on P_i×R^d for finite P_i⊂R^n. Write σ_Q for counting measure on Q times d-dimensional Lebesgue measure (counting on Q when d=0). Let γ_i≤a_iσ_{P_i}, 0<a_i<∞, let λ_i>0 sum to one and put P=Σλ_iP_i. For any old coupling there is a same-marginal coupling whose full physical barycentric law ρ dominates its old barycentric law in convex order and satisfies ρ≤A_dσ_P, with A_d=(Σλ_i a_i^(−1/d))^(−d) for d≥1 and A_0=min_i a_i. Each constant is sharp as a universal bound over common masses and supports. Every finite convex function on R^(n+d) is tested by the same selected coupling.

1bc960743a4bce34:03.reason: Every product tuple barycenter lies in C by convexity and its base belongs to the finite P. Thus this is a direct specialization of the same theorem, with no additional selection argument. Integer barycenters used by the old law alone do not guarantee integer barycenters under replacement. Convex order by itself compares no halfspace indicators and does not put the ordinary mean at an integer base.
1bc960743a4bce34:03.statement: For the finite-base convex-order selection with γ_i≤a_iσ_{P_i} supported in one compact convex set C⊂R^(n+d), if Σ_iλ_iP_i⊂Z^n, then the selected barycentric law is carried by C∩(Z^n×R^d) and has the bound A_d=(Σ_iλ_i a_i^(−1/d))^(−d) on each actual output fiber when d≥1 and the bound min_i a_i for counting measure when d=0. In particular equal weights 1/k with all P_i in one common residue class modulo kZ^n suffice, including the two-input equal-weight parity case. If a_i=1, the output is dominated by mixed volume on the actual output fibers.

732b11a769399016:02.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body with volume centroid $g$. For uniform $X$ on $K$, $u\ne0$, and $F(s)=\mathbb P(u\cdot(X-g)\ge s)$,
$$
F(s)+F(-s)\ge2\gamma_d\qquad(s\ge0).
$$
For $d\ge2$ the same bound holds with $F(s)=\mathbb P(Z\ge s)$ for any compactly supported, nonatomic, centered $1/d$-concave probability law of $Z$ on the line. In particular, for any independent random vector $Y\in\mathbb R^d$ with a distribution symmetric about zero, every closed halfspace through $g$ has $\mathbb P(X+Y\in H)\ge\gamma_d$. If $Y$ has finite first moment, the convolution has centroid $g$.

For a product of convex bodies $P\times K$ with $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ centrally symmetric about $j\in\mathbb Z^n$, every closed ambient halfspace containing $(j,g)$ has normalized mixed-integer mass at least $\gamma_d$.

ace4ff0d14f43769:4.statement:
Let $m,s\ge1$ be integers, let $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, and let $K\subset\mathbb R^s$ be a full-dimensional simplex of volume $V$ and centroid $c$. Put $\gamma_s=(s/(s+1))^s$, $Q_m=\{p\in\mathbb R^m:\sum_i |p_i|\le1\}$, $g(p)=(1+\sum_i p_i)/2$, and
$$
C=\{(p,u,x)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^s:
p\in Q_m,\ |u-g(p)|\le\varepsilon,\ x\in K\}.
$$
The body $C$ is full-dimensional. The coarse rule requires $p\in\mathbb Z^m$, with admissible set $S_{\mathrm c}=C\cap(\mathbb Z^m\times\mathbb R^{1+s})$ and measure $\mathcal H_{s+1}|_{S_{\mathrm c}}$. The fine rule additionally requires $u\in\mathbb Z$, with admissible set $S_{\mathrm f}=C\cap(\mathbb Z^{m+1}\times\mathbb R^s)$ and measure $\mathcal H_s|_{S_{\mathrm f}}$. For each rule normalize its measure by its own total mass. Define its maximum depth as the maximum over its admissible set of the infimum of normalized mass of all closed ambient halfspaces containing the point.

The coarse rule has $2m+1$ fibers of mass $2\varepsilon V$ and maximum depth $D_{\mathrm c}=\gamma_s$, attained at $(0,1/2,c)$. The fine rule has exactly $2m$ fibers of mass $V$, at $(e_i,1)$ and $(-e_i,0)$ for $1\le i\le m$, and maximum depth $D_{\mathrm f}=\gamma_s/(2m)$, attained at the centroid of each fiber. The ambient normalized laws are mutually singular. After projection to $(p,x)$, their total variation distance, defined by the supremum over measurable sets, is exactly $1/(2m+1)$, the coarse probability of the omitted base $p=0$.

The affine span of the fine bases has dimension $m$. Its integer points project bijectively to the odd-sum coset of the index-two even-sum sublattice of $\mathbb Z^m$. The fine mixed hull is $\operatorname{conv}(S_{\mathrm f})=\{(p,g(p),x):p\in Q_m,\ x\in K\}$ and has codimension one in $C$. Replacing $C$ by this hull preserves the fine set and fine measure and reduces the original coarse $\mathcal H_{s+1}$ mass to zero.

Thus for fixed $s$ and $\varepsilon$, a single added integer condition of projected index two gives $D_{\mathrm f}/D_{\mathrm c}=1/(2m)\to0$ with projected total variation tending to zero. In particular there is no positive dimension-independent retention factor for this comparison, even when the omitted coarse base marginal mass is arbitrarily small.

The deletion hulls of the witnesses lie in the respective convex sets, so their common intersection misses S. Conversely any k points with deletion hulls whose common intersection misses S give a critical family. For P_m, the simplex on 0 and the positive unit vectors has no other source point and its deletion hulls have empty common intersection. bd3988521f16dd20:1.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$, and let $u_1,\ldots,u_m$ be unit vectors. Write $H_i=\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge0\}$, $V=|K|$, and $\Phi(K)=\sum_i\theta_i|K\cap H_i|/V$ for weights $\theta_i>0$ with $\sum_i\theta_i=1$. Let $h$ be the support function of $K$ on the unit sphere. Take a nonzero $C^2$ function $\psi\ge0$ on the sphere such that on an open neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}\psi$, $h$ is $C^2$ and $A_h=\nabla_S^2 h+hI$ is positive definite on each spherical tangent space. Suppose the support points $X(n)=h(n)n+\nabla_S h(n)$ for $n\in\operatorname{supp}\psi$ satisfy $s_i u_i\cdot X(n)>0$ for fixed signs $s_i\in\{-1,1\}$ and every $i$.

For all sufficiently small signed $t$, $h_t=h+t\psi$ is the support function of a convex body $K_t$ with $0\in\operatorname{int}K_t$. The changed radial intervals are in $\{x:s_i u_i\cdot x>0\text{ for all }i\}$ and stay uniformly away from the cutting planes. In particular $K_t\cap u_i^\perp=K\cap u_i^\perp$ for all $i$. Set $V_t=|K_t|$, $\Delta V(t)=V_t-V$, $e_i=\mathbf1_{\{s_i=1\}}$, and $W=\sum_i\theta_i e_i$. Then
$$
|K_t\cap H_i|-|K\cap H_i|=e_i\Delta V(t),\qquad
\Phi(K_t)-\Phi(K)=(W-\Phi(K))\,\frac{\Delta V(t)}{V_t}.
$$
The volume $V_t$ is $C^1$ near $0$, $\Delta V(t)$ has the sign of $t$ for $t\ne0$, and
$$
V'_0=\int_{\partial K}\psi(n(x))\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}(x)>0
$$
where $n(x)$ is the outward unit normal wherever it is unique.

At a Hausdorff local minimum of $\Phi$ subject to the same section traces, every such patch has $W=\Phi(K)$. Group the $u_i$ by their unoriented planes. A positive-curvature patch crossing exactly one such plane at a point on no other distinct plane excludes a local minimum if the two orientations in that class have unequal total weights. If $h$ is $C^2$ and $A_h>0$ on the entire sphere, an imbalanced class always gives such a patch. If all classes balance, $\Phi(K)=1/2$ for every $K$.

bd3988521f16dd20:4.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$. Suppose the $d+1$ unit vectors $u_i$ span $\mathbb R^d$ and form a minimal positive circuit, and that $\theta_i>0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$ satisfy $\sum_i\theta_i S_i u_i=0$, where $S_i=\mathcal H^{d-1}(K\cap u_i^\perp)$. As in the stationary setting, suppose the sections have centroid $0$. Assume the central cap masses $|K\cap\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge0\}|$ all equal $Q$, where $Q$ is the maximum over $y\in K$ of $\inf_{H\ni y}|K\cap H|$ for closed halfspaces $H$. Then the selected caps attain the depth at the deepest point $0$.

Take a bump $K_t$ as in the section-preserving support-bump lemma with signature weight $W\ne Q/|K|$. Such a bump exists if $h$ is $C^2$ with everywhere positive-definite $A_h$. For small signed $t$ there are a point $y(t)$ near $0$ and $d+1$ parallel translates of the respective original caps through $y(t)$, all with the same mass $q(t)$. They cover $\mathbb R^d$ and bound the new maximum raw depth by $q(t)$. The normalized cover bound has derivative
$$
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\frac{q(t)}{|K_t|}\right|_{t=0}
=\left(W-\frac Q{|K|}\right)\frac{V'_0}{|K|}.
$$
For all sufficiently small nonzero $t$ of the appropriate sign, the maximal normalized ordinary depth of $K_t$ is strictly below that of $K$.

Integrating the even cosine powers gives $\int\psi=\pi/16$, $\int\psi^2=35\pi/768$ and $\int(\psi')^2=15\pi/4$. The normalized derivative uses $W=1/3$, $Q/|K|=1/2$ and $V'(0)=\pi/16$. cd833c78fb705a2e:01.statement:
Let $D\ge1$, let $\mu$ be a finite nonnegative Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}^D$ with convex support $K=\operatorname{supp}\mu$, and suppose every affine hyperplane has zero $\mu$-mass. Assume there is a fixed $g>0$ such that every closed convex subset $L\subseteq K$ of positive $\mu$-mass contains a point $y$ satisfying $\mu(L\cap H)\ge g\mu(L)$ for every closed halfspace $H$ containing $y$.

Let $H_1,\ldots,H_m$ be a finite cover of $K$ by closed halfspaces with nonzero normals, with $m\ge1$, and let $A_i=\mu(H_i)$. For every $\alpha\ge0$,
$$
\mu(K)\le\sum_{i=1}^m(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \frac{\alpha}{g},
\qquad x_+=\max\{x,0\}.
\tag{1}
$$

For ordinary volume on a convex body $K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^D$, write $V=\operatorname{vol}_D(K)$ and $\gamma_D=(D/(D+1))^D$. Then (1) holds with $g=\gamma_D$ and $A_i=\operatorname{vol}_D(K\cap H_i)$. In particular, for $a=\min_i A_i$,
$$
\sum_{i=1}^m A_i-V\ge(m-1/\gamma_D)a.
\tag{2}
$$
Arrange the cap masses in decreasing order and append zeros if $m<3$. For $D\ge2$,
$$
A_{(1)}+A_{(2)}+(1/\gamma_D-2)A_{(3)}\ge V,
\tag{3}
$$
where $0<1/\gamma_D-2<1$. For $D=1$, $A_{(1)}+A_{(2)}\ge V$.

d0cb383fd9782a9f:02.statement:
Let $C=\{(z,x)\in\mathbb R^2:0\le z\le2,\ 0\le x\le z+1\}$ and let $\mu$ be the restriction of $\mathcal H_1$ to $C\cap(\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R)$, equivalently the sum of the lengths on the three integer fibers. Suppose at most two closed convex subsets of $C$, each of positive $\mu$-mass, partition the mixed set up to $\mu$-null omissions and overlaps, and each has a true mixed centroid with integer base coordinate. Then there are exactly two pieces, $D$ and $E$, of masses $4$ and $2$ and base centroid coordinates $1$ and $2$, respectively. The true mixed centroid $y_D=\mu(D)^{-1}\int_D (z,x)\,d\mu$ lies on the boundary of a closed ambient halfspace $H$ with $\mu(D\cap H)=7/4$ and $\mu(E\cap H)=0$. Hence its normalized halfspace depth in $D$ is at most $7/16<\gamma_1=1/2$.

Such partitions exist even with full-dimensional pieces covering all of $C$. This body therefore disproves the assertion that every mixed-integer convex body admits an exhaustive partition into at most $2^n$ positive-mass closed convex pieces whose true mixed centroids have integer bases and each have normalized depth at least $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ within their own pieces.

dafd411c026c302c:1.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional convex body, $d\ge1$, with volume $V$ and centroid $g$. For $u\ne0$ write $F(s)=|K\cap\{x:u\cdot(x-g)\ge s\}|/V$, and set $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. For every $s\in\mathbb R$,
$$
F(0)+F(s)+\frac12F(-s)\ge\gamma_d+\frac12.
$$
The right-hand side is attained. Equivalently, for every Lebesgue-measurable $A\subseteq K$ of volume $a$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$
|K\cap\{u\cdot(x-g)\ge0\}|+
|A\cap\{u\cdot(x-g)\ge t\}|+
|K\cap\{u\cdot(x-g)\ge-t\}|
\ge \gamma_d V+\frac a2.
$$

dafd411c026c302c:5.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, and let $A,B,C\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies with $(A+C)/2\subseteq B$. Set $S=(\{-1\}\times A)\cup(\{0\}\times B)\cup(\{1\}\times C)$, measured by summing $d$-dimensional volumes on its three fibers. If a convex body $K$ satisfies $A\subseteq K\subseteq B\cap C$, let $a=|A|$, $V=|K|$, $E=|B|+|C|-2V$ and let $g_K$ be the volume centroid of $K$. Then the actual point $(0,g_K)$ has normalized mixed halfspace depth at least
$$
\frac{\gamma_d V+a/2}{2V+E+a}.
$$
This is at least $\gamma_d/2$ if $E\le(1/\gamma_d-1)a$. In particular, for $B=C=K$ the displayed bound holds with $E=0$, and the same conclusion holds at the actual middle centroid when $B$ and $C$ are translates of one another, taking $V=|B|$.

If $A,B,C$ are totally ordered by inclusion, some actual mixed point has normalized depth at least $\gamma_d/2$. The same holds if such an order is obtained by an affine change preserving $\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R^d$, including a shear affine in the integer base.

e4ccf81294305ade:09.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$ and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body. For $z\in\mathbb Z^n$ write $K_z=\{y:(z,y)\in C\}$ and let $g_z$ be its volume centroid when $|K_z|>0$. Fix an integer base $w$ with $|K_w|>0$. For any finite convex representation
$$
(w,x)=\sum_i\lambda_i(z_i,g_{z_i}),\qquad
\lambda_i>0,\quad \sum_i\lambda_i=1,\quad |K_{z_i}|>0,
$$
set $a=(\sum_i\lambda_i|K_{z_i}|^{1/d})^d$ and $\delta=1-a/|K_w|\in[0,1)$. For a nonzero linear functional $u$ on $\mathbb R^d$ let $W=\max_{K_w}u-\min_{K_w}u$. Then
$$
\frac{|u(x-g_w)|}{W}
\le \min\left\{\delta,\ \frac{d}{d+1}\frac{\delta}{1-\delta},\ \frac{d}{d+1}\right\}.
$$
For $0\le\varepsilon<1$, let $S_\varepsilon(w)$ be the set of all $x$ admitting such a representation with $a\ge (1-\varepsilon)|K_w|$. The width of $u(S_\varepsilon(w))$ is at most $\frac{\varepsilon}{1-\varepsilon}W$.

For every $d\ge1$ and $0<\delta<1$, an actual body with $n=1$, three integer fibers, and a representation at $w=0$ attains
$$
\frac{u(x-g_w)}{W}=\frac{d}{d+1}\frac{\delta(1-\delta^{1/d})}{1-\delta}.
$$
Consequently the coefficient $d/(d+1)$ is optimal to first order as $\delta\downarrow0$, even for such bodies. For every $d\ge1$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$, an actual body with $n=2$, five integer fibers, and $w=0$ has width $\varepsilon W$ for $u(S_\varepsilon(0))$. Thus the width coefficient one is optimal to first order as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$.

edf02845b3275e8c:02.statement:
Let $n,d$ be positive integers and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body. Put $\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $S=C\cap\Lambda$, and assume $q=\dim_{\mathrm H}S\ge 1$. Set $\mu=\mathcal H_q|_S$. For $z\in\mathbb Z^n$ put $K_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$, and let $P=\{z:w_z=\mathcal H_q(K_z)>0\}$.

Suppose finitely many labeled mass and base moment pairs $(t_i,m_i)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n$ are feasible: there are $s_{iz}\ge 0$ with $\sum_i s_{iz}=w_z$ for $z\in P$ and $(t_i,m_i)=\sum_{z\in P}s_{iz}(1,z)$ for every label. Discard the labels with $t_i=0$ and index the remaining $k$ labels by $1,\ldots,k$. Fix any vectors $u_i\in\mathbb R^d$ such that $x\mapsto(u_i-u_j)\cdot x$ is nonconstant on each $K_z$ for $z\in P$ whenever $i\ne j$.

There are finite $\theta_i\in\mathbb R^{n+1}$ such that the affine scores $L_i(z,x)=\theta_i\cdot(1,z)+u_i\cdot x$ give closed cells
$$
D_i=C\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{(z,x):L_i(z,x)\ge L_j(z,x)\}.
$$
Each $D_i$ is an ambient convex body cut from $C$ by at most $k-1$ closed halfspaces, and $D_i\cap\Lambda$ has Hausdorff dimension $q$. The cells satisfy
$$
\bigcup_iD_i=C,\qquad
\mu(D_i\cap D_j)=0\quad(i\ne j),\qquad
\left(\mu(D_i),\int_{D_i} z\,d\mu\right)=(t_i,m_i).
$$
In particular they exhaust the mixed measure. The centroid of $\mathcal H_q|_{D_i\cap\Lambda}$ belongs to $D_i$, has base $m_i/t_i$, and lies in $D_i\cap\Lambda$ if that base is integral. Suitable $u_i$ always exist.

edf02845b3275e8c:07.statement:
Let $n,d$ be positive integers and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body. Write $\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $S=C\cap\Lambda$, and assume $q=\dim_{\mathrm H}S\ge1$. Then $C$ is the union of $k\le2^n$ closed affine-score winner cells that are ambient convex bodies, each cut from $C$ by at most $k-1$ closed halfspaces. Every mixed piece $D_i\cap\Lambda$ has dimension $q$ and positive $\mathcal H_q$ measure. Distinct mixed pieces overlap in $\mathcal H_q$-null sets. The actual centroid of $\mathcal H_q|_{D_i\cap\Lambda}$ belongs to $D_i\cap\Lambda$, and the distinct centroid bases are exactly the vertices and all the lattice points of their convex hull. In particular $\sum_i\mathcal H_q(D_i\cap\Lambda)=\mathcal H_q(S)$.

The universal count $2^n$ is sharp already for $q=d$, even if fractional splitting of the mixed measure is allowed instead of convex cells.

f62fe2e83b180bf3:01.statement: For d≥1, m≥1 and any probability law of Ξ on the standard m-coordinate simplex, define φ(x)=inf_{t>0, Pr(x·Ξ≤t)>0} t/Pr(x·Ξ≤t)^(1/d) for x∈R^m_+. Then φ is coordinatewise nondecreasing, positively homogeneous, continuous on the whole orthant, and bounded above by max_j x_j. For each fixed finite number of rows and each fixed list of weights c_i≥0, H_c(X)=Σ_i c_i φ(X_i) attains its maximum over nonnegative matrices with m columns summing individually to one, and has a maximizer with a minimum number of nonzero rows.

f62fe2e83b180bf3:03.statement: Let X maximize H_c of §1, and let its fully positive row r have c_r>0. For every v in the span of the active rows choose a_i with v+Σ_i a_iX_i=0. If φ is differentiable at X_r and s=t/(1+ta_r), the exact total objective remainder is H_c(X(t))−H_c(X)=c_r(1+ta_r)[φ(X_r+sv)−φ(X_r)−sDφ(X_r)[v]]. Thus every existing second directional coefficient in the active-row span is nonpositive, and a strict increase over the tangent at arbitrarily small feasible s contradicts maximality. At a minimum-active maximizer with k active rows, a p-dimensional positive-definite Hessian subspace of such a row is impossible when k+p>m. In particular k=m excludes every such row that has a positive second direction.

For either state X write S_X=Σ_Xℓ_z², T_X=Σ_X r_zℓ_z and M=T_I+T_J. Then S_I=3T_I−(1−θ)M and S_J=3T_J−θM. In every strict trace cell the Hessian is Σ_I v_zv_zᵀ/(1−θ)−Σ_J v_zv_zᵀ/θ, and is positive semidefinite at a local minimum.

f89d52b54ff6950f:3.statement: If the radii extend to a concave function on conv(P), then at such an interior stationary point M≤r_z0 Σℓ_z and Σℓ_z²≤2r_z0 Σℓ_z. For θ<1/2, every strict J index satisfies α·(z−z0)>(1−2θ)r_z>0.

f89d52b54ff6950f:4.reason: Finite tilt clamping and strict improvement eliminate purely integer directions. In the interior angular chart stationary endpoints have equal positive width and must lie strictly in states I,J. The α-curvature, Hessian determinant, and one-sided second variation at θ=1/2 exclude every interior angle. Accepted 2a8c2bc6d7992c5e covers compact tilt reduction for compatible planar slices but supplies no angular classification.
f89d52b54ff6950f:4.statement: For any a,b,c>0 and centered triangle fibers aT,cT,bT at bases −1,0,1, the depth at (0,0) is attained by a through-source cap. Every minimizing cap has nonzero continuous normal in a canonical vertex direction or its opposite, with no assumption c≥(a+b)/2.

f89d52b54ff6950f:5.reason: The only interior quadratic minimum occurs at α=a−b and is feasible exactly for a/2≤b≤2a. Saturation plateaus and full transitions give the other extrema. Complementarity gives the opposite-direction minimum and §2 closes the angular search.
f89d52b54ff6950f:5.statement: For r>0 let f_r(k) be 0 for k≤−2r, (2r+k)^2/2 for −2r≤k≤r, and (9/2)r² for k≥r. For g(α)=f_a(−α)+f_b(α), a,b>0, min g=min{(a+b)^2,(9/2)a²,(9/2)b²} and max g=max{(9/2)a²+(2b−a)_+²/2,(9/2)b²+(2a−b)_+²/2}. For any c>0 the middle depth is the smaller of 2c²+min g and (5/2)c²+(9/2)(a²+b²)−max g.

f89d52b54ff6950f:6.reason: Shift the integer bases by one. Convexity forces the midpoint inclusion, which for homothetic copies of the same nondegenerate triangle is precisely c≥(a+b)/2. The accepted lifted-hull construction proves sufficiency and accounts for all integer bases.
f89d52b54ff6950f:6.statement: Centered triangle fibers aT,cT,bT at bases −1,0,1 with positive radii are realized as exactly the integer fibers of a convex body if and only if c≥(a+b)/2.

f89d52b54ff6950f:7.reason: The two scalar minima from §3 differ strictly in favor of the canonical branch. For a≤b<2a the two difference lower bounds in (18) cover complementary ratio ranges, and for b≥2a the difference is c²/2.
f89d52b54ff6950f:7.statement: If a,b,c>0 and c≥(a+b)/2, then the middle centroid raw depth is D0=2c²+min{(a+b)^2,(9/2)a²,(9/2)b²}, and every minimizing continuous normal is one of the three canonical vertex directions.

f89d52b54ff6950f:8.reason: Convex depth superlevels contain the average of the triangle-symmetry orbit. Finite tilts isolate an endpoint while preserving its ordinary cut. The exact middle formula supplies the remaining candidate for the maximum.
f89d52b54ff6950f:8.statement: For the compatible three centered homothets, the centroid maximizes depth within each fiber. At either endpoint base the depth at every point equals its ordinary depth in that triangle, with centroid depth 2a² or 2b². Thus the global raw depth is max{2a²,2b²,D0}, with normalized depth obtained by division by (9/2)(a²+c²+b²).

f89d52b54ff6950f:9.reason: Apply the planar three-positive-fiber theorem to the three midpoint-compatible triangle fibers after shifting the bases. The theorem is for arbitrary planar shapes and therefore gives the same 2/9 bound on this subclass.
f89d52b54ff6950f:9.statement: The maximum normalized depth of every compatible three-centered-homothet body above is at least 2/9.

external_dependencies: Ordinary d-dimensional Brunn–Minkowski for nonempty compact convex caps. R. J. Gardner, The Brunn–Minkowski Inequality, Bull. AMS 39 (2002), Theorem 4.1.
f8e965b8e4034ce3:01.reason: The addend preserves integer bases and every old cap fiber plus the addend's centroid cap stays in the translated new cap. Apply full-mass Grünbaum to that centroid cap and ordinary Brunn–Minkowski to the positive-volume old cap fibers. Expansion of the integer power and Σ f_i^p≥(Σ f_i)^p for 0<p≤1 give the raw root increment. If the old cap has zero mixed volume, the chosen actual fiber alone contains the translated addend cap. Vertical caps take whole included fibers. For sharpness every cube vertex is an exposed integer index, hence an arbitrarily prescribed own-fiber cap can be isolated by finite base tilt. The simplex direction of ea91e021ff1f4416 gives the matching own-fiber maximum, while Grünbaum gives the centroid lower bound.
f8e965b8e4034ce3:01.statement: Let n≥0, d≥1 and C⊂ℝⁿ×ℝᵈ be a compact convex body with a nonempty integer fiber, and let L⊂ℝᵈ be a convex body of volume ℓ>0 and centroid g_L. For t≥0 put C_t=C+({0}×tL), S_t=C_t∩(ℤⁿ×ℝᵈ), let D_t be raw mixed d-volume depth on S_t, and let D_*(t)=sup_{y∈S_t} D_t(y). For s,t≥0 and every y∈S_t, D_{t+s}(y+(0,sg_L))^(1/d)≥D_t(y)^(1/d)+sΓ_d^(1/d)ℓ^(1/d), where Γ_d=(d/(d+1))ᵈ. Consequently D_*(t+s)^(1/d)≥D_*(t)^(1/d)+sΓ_d^(1/d)ℓ^(1/d). This includes zero initial d-volume and has sharp additive coefficient for every n,d. For a d-simplex L and C=[0,1]ⁿ×εL with ε>0, one has D_*(t)=Γ_d(ε+t)ᵈℓ, with the same formula for n=0 taking C=εL.

This is a consequence of that exact depth computation, not a dependency of the growth theorem above. The normalized dip and the nonconcavity of the raw root concern different functions.
f8e965b8e4034ce3:02.statement: For the common vertical addition from the lifted hull of [0,1],[0,5],[0,1] at −1,0,1 with addend L=[−1,1], the raw maximum depth, which is already its own root when d=1, is 3+2t on 0≤t≤1/2 and (5+6t)/2 on t≥1/2. It is not concave in t; its two slopes are 2 and 3.

ff31d56304dd901a:01.reason: The accepted ordinary theorem states the rigidity, continuity and uniform normalization. With the stated translations the midpoint inclusion gives C⊂2B, and |C| converges to |T|. The theorem's bounded-partner clause then makes the maximum inscribed volume tend to |T|, uniformly for all these partners.
ff31d56304dd901a:01.statement: Ordinary maximal depth of a full-dimensional convex body is continuous under Hausdorff convergence to a full-dimensional body, is at least $\Gamma_d$, and equals $\Gamma_d$ exactly for a simplex. Mapping a maximal inscribed simplex to the standard simplex $T$ gives $T\subset B\subset[-1,1]^d$ and uniform convergence to $T$ as $D(B)\downarrow\Gamma_d$. For pairs $(A,C)$ with $(A+C)/2\subset B$, translate them oppositely so that $0\in A$. If $D(C)\to\Gamma_d$ and $|C|/|B|\to1$ uniformly, then the maximal inscribed-simplex volume of the translated $C$ divided by $|B|$ tends to one uniformly.

ff31d56304dd901a:02.reason: The accepted finite-star result has the same hypotheses, value of α and all-tilt conclusion. The determinant, endpoint credit and proper-section controls are in its checked dependency chain. Its proof has the same normalized displacement and a coarea error proportional to the total small-pair mass.
ff31d56304dd901a:02.statement: For $d\ge2$ set $N=d+1$, $J=\lceil N/2\rceil$ and $\alpha=(\Gamma_d+J/N)/2$. There is $\theta_d>0$ such that whenever finitely many full-dimensional endpoint pairs obey $(A_j+C_j)/2\subset B$, $D(B),D(C_j)\le\Gamma_d(1+\theta_d)$, $(1+\theta_d)^{-1}\le |C_j|/|B|\le1+\theta_d$, and $0<e=\sum_j|A_j|\le\theta_d|B|$, one center in $\operatorname{int}B$ gives total mass at least $\Gamma_d|B|+\alpha e$ in the middle cap and the two endpoint caps with opposite arbitrary shifts per pair, for every nonconstant affine functional. A whole-middle cap also suffices after decreasing $\theta_d$.

ff31d56304dd901a:03.reason: The grouping paragraph of the accepted proof proves this standalone step under exactly E<2^{-d}m. A fixed point in the outside fiber makes a half-scale copy of the partner fit inside the integer midpoint fiber. Its volume forces the midpoint into the core. Parity then determines v from p and w follows.
ff31d56304dd901a:03.statement: If a mixed convex body has a complete parity transversal of positive fibers with smallest volume $m$ and outside volume $E<2^{-d}m$, every nonempty outside fiber, including a null fiber, has a unique base expression $p=2w-v$ for distinct core bases $v,w$, with $v$ its parity partner. Within each target group the core partners are distinct and the two thresholds of a through-target cap have opposite shifts.

ff31d56304dd901a:04.reason: The accepted statement uses exactly this core and this outside-mass normalization. In the failure argument the core maxima and volumes satisfy the star hypothesis, and the average of the repaired point guarantees is at least the target, strictly greater in that argument when E>0. The E=0 case uses the largest core fiber.
ff31d56304dd901a:04.statement: For every $d\ge2$ there exists $\rho_d>0$ independent of $n\ge1$ such that an actual convex mixed source with one positive core fiber from each parity class and total outside volume at most $\rho_d$ times the smallest core volume has a mixed point of normalized depth at least $\Gamma_d/2^n$.

ff5285005955b0c7:01.reason: The ball construction, outer slice convergence and all-halfspace estimates together give a citable conditional depth reduction without boundary-null assumptions. Upper semicontinuity uses the same fixed-measure argument as the accepted attainment fact, but its proof here covers all ambient points and axes. Historical reviews f638b5311f3edc75 and ea9523dad40d704c check the finite-net geometry and exact denominators. No attainment of an extremal body in the strict class is claimed.
ff5285005955b0c7:01.statement: Let C be a convex body in R^n×R^d, n+d≥1, with positive mixed d-volume M. With C⊂R B_{n+d}, R≥1, and U_k a finite 1/k-net containing all signed coordinate directions, put T_k=k(R²+1)+R and C_k=∩_{u∈U_k}B(−T_k u,T_k+h_C(u)+1/k). Then C⊂int C_k, C_k is strictly convex, and d_H(C_k,C)≤[1+√(n+d)(R+1)+R]/k. Eventually the nonempty integer bases are exactly those of C. Every original nonempty fiber is full-dimensional in C_k and converges in Hausdorff distance to its original fiber. The mixed d-volume measures μ_k and μ satisfy sup_A |μ_k(A)−μ(A)|=δ_k=M_k−M→0 over Borel A. If A_ν(y)=inf_{H∋y}ν(H) over closed ambient halfspaces, then sup_y |A_{μ_k}(y)/M_k−A_μ(y)/M|≤δ_k/M_k. Any subsequential limit of points y_k in the mixed source of C_k with normalized depth≥c lies in the mixed source of C and has normalized depth≥c. For d≥2 every fiber in C_k of positive d-volume meets each supporting hyperplane in an H_{d-1}-null set. For d=1 every interval has endpoint H_0 mass one, while for d=0 the counting measures eventually coincide.

ff5285005955b0c7:02.reason: Direct counterexample to dropping outer containment from the measure-convergence argument. It is a scope check for the preceding construction.
ff5285005955b0c7:02.statement: For n=1 and any d-dimensional convex body K of d-volume one, C=[0,1]×K and C_k=[1/k,1+1/k]×K, k≥2, converge in Hausdorff distance, yet the mixed masses are respectively two and one. For d≥2 one can take K to be a Euclidean ball, so strict positive fibers alone do not repair this failure.

ff5285005955b0c7:03.statement: Fix n≥0 and d≥2 and a convex body C with nonempty mixed source S of dimension q=dim_H S. Suppose every convex body of positive mixed d-volume whose positive integer fibers are strictly convex and H_{d−1}-null on all supporting hyperplanes has a mixed point of normalized closed-halfspace depth at least c. Then C has a mixed point of normalized H_q depth at least the same c. More precisely for ε_j=1/j there are strictly convex ambient outer bodies B_j of the vertical tube A_j=C+({0}^n×ε_j B_d) with d_H(B_j,A_j)≤ε_j and extra mixed d-volume at most ε_j times the mass of A_j. Their normalized mixed measures converge weakly to H_q|_S/H_q(S) and d_H(B_j,C)≤2ε_j.
